condition: Suxamethonium apnoea history before emergency surgery (butyrylcholinesterase deficiency)
permutationLabel: Suxamethonium apnoea, emergency appendicectomy with RSI
summary: 45-year-old woman with prolonged paralysis after suxamethonium at a previous caesarean section now needs emergency laparoscopic appendicectomy (rapid sequence induction).

inputs.hpi: 30 hours of pain starting around the umbilicus and moving to the right iliac fossa, anorexia, one vomit. At a caesarean section in 2012 she stayed on a ventilator for 6 hours after the anaesthetic and was told she has 'suxamethonium sensitivity'; carries a card. Urine pregnancy test negative today.

exam.general: HR 98, BP 124/78, RR 18, SpO2 98% on air, T 37.9°C.
exam.abdomen: Tender at McBurney's point with localised guarding. Rovsing's positive.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Non-compressible appendix 9 mm with periappendiceal fat stranding. Ovaries normal.

comorbidities: Suxamethonium apnoea (butyrylcholinesterase deficiency) — prolonged ventilation after suxamethonium 2012

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute appendicitis — emergency laparoscopic appendicectomy; history of suxamethonium apnoea
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute appendicitis for emergency laparoscopic appendicectomy. Previous suxamethonium apnoea (probable butyrylcholinesterase deficiency) — avoid suxamethonium and mivacurium.

guideline.name: Butyrylcholinesterase deficiency and its clinical importance in anaesthesia (systematic review)
guideline.section: Prolonged neuromuscular block after suxamethonium or mivacurium; avoid both in known or suspected deficiency; test the patient and relatives
guideline.citation: Andersson ML, Møller AM, Wildgaard K. Anaesthesia. 2019;74:518–28.

guideline.name: Association of Anaesthetists guideline — malignant hyperthermia 2020
guideline.section: MH-susceptible patients and untested first-degree relatives of an MH-susceptible patient: trigger-free anaesthesia (no volatile agents, no suxamethonium), dantrolene immediately available, refer relatives to an MH unit for testing
guideline.citation: Hopkins PM, Girard T, Dalay S, et al. Malignant hyperthermia 2020: Guideline from the Association of Anaesthetists. Anaesthesia. 2021;76:655–64.

rationale: Permutation of the MH vignette: a different inherited anaesthetic hazard, in an emergency. The history is in the PMH and HPI; the check is whether any output surfaces it and adapts the RSI plan. Appendicectomy is correct here.
